editorial.tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose grouping of RL items, not one developing story. Since Oct 12 it has collected a Qwen long-horizon agent report, an O-RAN benchmark, and four Oct 20-22 arXiv papers on training tool-using and search agents.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 23: AWS publishes a hands-on guide to multi-turn RL on Amazon SageMaker AI, training on whole-task outcomes with a Wordle example.
editorial.why_it_matters: The SageMaker guide is the first managed-platform recipe in the thread, so teams on AWS can try outcome-based multi-turn RL without building the training harness. The arXiv papers cover rollout cost, stateful environments, search-state awareness and per-decision credit assignment; QwenGyre (a secondary-source report) and X-RIC remain research or telecom-specific.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you train tool-using models, read the rollout-budget and twin-world credit-assignment papers for cheaper, finer-grained learning signal; if you run on AWS, try the SageMaker Wordle pipeline before planning around it, and wait for Qwen's primary QwenGyre release.

Does BIRD-RL's gain on small language models hold on larger models?

Does the SageMaker MTRL recipe carry from Wordle to tool-using agent tasks, and at what training cost?
